1.note: Isaiah is speaking to the **nations** and the **peoples** that he knows cannot hear him. He is doing this to communicate to the people listening to him that he feels very strongly about the judgment that Yahweh is about to bring on all the earth. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate these words as if he were speaking directly to the people about the nations and the peoples. Alternate translation: [I am calling the nations to come near and hear, and the peoples to pay attention]

1.q: תִּשְׁמַ֤ע הָ⁠אָ֨רֶץ֙ וּ⁠מְלֹאָ֔⁠הּ תֵּבֵ֖ל וְ⁠כָל צֶאֱצָאֶֽי⁠הָ
1.note: Isaiah is speaking to the **earth** and the **world** that he knows cannot hear him. He is doing this to communicate to the people listening to him that he feels very strongly about the judgment that Yahweh is about to bring. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate these words as if he were speaking directly to the people about the earth and the world. Alternate translation: [I want all the people on earth to hear, everybody, even their children]

Isaiah is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [let the world and all of its offspring hear]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **fullness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and all that fills it]

2.note: The word translated as **For** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [The reason for this is that]

Isaiah is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and his wrath is against all of their army]

The terms **fury** and **wrath** mean similar things. Isaiah is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [Yahweh is very angry against all of the nations, and his greatest anger is against all of their army]

3.note: The expression **will be thrown out** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [No one will bury their slain]

Isaiah is using the adjective **slain** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [And their slain ones]

The expression **will be melted** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and their blood will melt the mountains]

Isaiah says **the mountains will be melted with their blood** as an extreme statement for emphasis. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [and so much blood will flow that even the mountains will be covered with it]

4.note: The expression **will be dissolved** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [And all of the army of the heavens will dissolve]

Isaiah is speaking as if the stars were **the army of the heavens**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And all of the stars, the army of the heavens, will dissolve]

The expression **will be rolled up** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and the heavens will roll up like a scroll]

The point of this comparison is that just as **a scroll** is rolled up so that it can no longer be seen, so **the heavens** will vanish from sight. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [and the heavens will vanish from sight just as a scroll is rolled up and can no longer be seen]

4.q: וְ⁠כָל צְבָאָ֣⁠ם יִבּ֔וֹל כִּ⁠נְבֹ֤ל עָלֶה֙ מִ⁠גֶּ֔פֶן וּ⁠כְ⁠נֹבֶ֖לֶת מִ⁠תְּאֵנָֽה
4.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **a leaf** withers and falls from **a vine**, so **all of their army** will fade away and disappear. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [and all of their army will wither and disappear just as a leaf withers and falls from a vine and just as leaves wither and fall from a fig tree]
The pronoun **their** refers to the heavens. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and all of the army of the heavens will wither]

5.q: כִּֽי־רִוְּתָ֥ה בַ⁠שָּׁמַ֖יִם חַרְבִּ֑⁠י הִנֵּה֙ עַל־אֱד֣וֹם תֵּרֵ֔ד וְ⁠עַל־עַ֥ם חֶרְמִ֖⁠י לְ⁠מִשְׁפָּֽט
5.note: This verse is a direct quotation of Yahweh. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could mark this as a direct quotation of him. The UST models one way to do that.

Here the word **For** introduces not a reason but an explanation. Yahweh means that now that he has defeated the “army of the heavens,” as the preceding verse describes, he will execute judgment on earthly powers. Alternate translation: [Now that]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [my sword has slaked its thirst in the heavens]

Yahweh is speaking of his **sword** as if it were a living thing that could have **slaked** its thirst until it was satisfied. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I have defeated the heavenly powers with my sword]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **people** that are characterized as ones he will devote to **to judgment**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the people whom I will devote to judgment]

6.q: חֶ֣רֶב לַ⁠יהוָ֞ה מָלְאָ֥ה דָם֙ הֻדַּ֣שְׁנָה מֵ⁠חֵ֔לֶב
6.note: Isaiah is speaking of **the sword of Yahweh** as if it were a living thing that could fill and get fat. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Yahweh has killed many with his sword, so that it is covered with blood and fat]

6.q: הֻדַּ֣שְׁנָה מֵ⁠חֵ֔לֶב מִ⁠דַּ֤ם כָּרִים֙ וְ⁠עַתּוּדִ֔ים מֵ⁠חֵ֖לֶב כִּלְי֣וֹת אֵילִ֑ים
6.note: Isaiah is speaking as if the people of Edom were like sacrificial animals such as **lambs**, **goats**, and **rams**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [as if the Edomites were sacrificial animals whom it had slaughtered and whose fat and blood were covering it]

The word translated as **For** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [This is because]

6.q: כִּ֣י זֶ֤בַח לַֽ⁠יהוָה֙ בְּ⁠בָצְרָ֔ה וְ⁠טֶ֥בַח גָּד֖וֹל בְּ⁠אֶ֥רֶץ אֱדֽוֹם
6.note: Isaiah is speaking of the **slaughter ** of the people of **Edom** as if it were **a sacrifice** that Yahweh offers. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [For Yahweh will slaughter many people in Bozrah, and there will be a great slaughter in the land of Edom]

Isaiah is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and there will be a great slaughter in the land of Edom]

7.q: וְ⁠יָרְד֤וּ רְאֵמִים֙ עִמָּ֔⁠ם וּ⁠פָרִ֖ים עִם אַבִּירִ֑ים
7.note: Isaiah is speaking as if the strong warriors of Edom were **wild oxen** and **young bulls**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And the strong warriors of Edom will fall together with the young warriors]

Isaiah is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and young bulls will go down with the strong bulls]

Isaiah is using the adjective **strong** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [the strong bulls]

Isaiah is speaking of **their land** as if it were a living thing that could drink until it was satisfied. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And their land will be soaked with blood]

The expression **will be fattened** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and their dust will become rich with fat]
This is poetic language. If your language has a way to indicate poetry, you could use it here. Alternate translation: [and fat will saturate their dust]

8.note: The word translated as **For** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [This is because]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **vengeance**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [a day when Yahweh takes revenge]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **retribution**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [a year when he punishes them]

Isaiah is using the possessive form to describe a **cause** that is characterized by **Zion**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [for the cause of defending Zion]

9.note: The expression **will be turned** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [And its streams will turn into pitch]

Isaiah is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and its dust will be turned into sulfur] or [and its dust will turn into sulfur]

10.note: Isaiah is referring to all of the time by naming its two major components, **Night** and **day**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [Always it will not be extinguished] or [It will never stop burning]
The pronoun **it** refers to the burning land of Edom. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the fire of Edom will not extinguish; its smoke]

Isaiah says **its smoke will rise forever** as an extreme statement for emphasis. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [its smoke will never stop rising]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **generation**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [Always and forever]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **perpetuity**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [forever and ever]

Isaiah is repeating forms of the word **perpetuity** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [forever and ever]

11.note: The **pelican** and the **desert owl** are kinds of birds. If your readers would not be familiar with what they are, you could use the names of similar birds that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [And kinds of birds known as the pelican and the desert owl]

The **screech owl** and the **raven** are kinds of birds. If your readers would not be familiar with what they are, you could use the names of similar birds that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [and kinds of birds known as the screech owl and the raven]
The pronoun **he** refers to Yahweh. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And Yahweh will stretch over it]

Isaiah is speaking as if Yahweh would mark out Edom for ruin with a **measuring line of formlessness** and **the stones of emptiness**, using building tools to lay out chaos and emptiness rather than a city. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [complete ruin and emptiness]

Isaiah is using the possessive form to describe a measuring **line** that is characterized by **formlessness**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the measuring line that marks out the lack of anything that has form]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **formlessness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [what has no form]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **emptiness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [an empty place]

Isaiah is speaking of **stones of emptiness **as if Yahweh could stretch a measuring line over them. If this image communicates well in your language, please use it. If not, you could express this as a comparison. Alternate translation: [and the desolation of the land]

12.note: This exaggerates the princes losing their royal status by saying that they will become **nothing**. Alternate translation: [all her princes will no longer rule]

13.q: וְ⁠עָלְתָ֤ה אַרְמְנֹתֶ֨י⁠הָ֙ סִירִ֔ים קִמּ֥וֹשׂ וָ⁠ח֖וֹחַ בְּ⁠מִבְצָרֶ֑י⁠הָ
13.note: Isaiah is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [And thorns will come up in her palaces, and the nettle and the thornbush will come up in her fortifications]
The pronoun **her** refers to Edom. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [in Edom’s palaces … in Edom’s fortifications]

The **nettle** and the **thornbush** are kinds of thorny plants. If your readers would not be familiar with what they are, you could use the names of similar plants that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [thorny weeds and thornbushes]

Isaiah is speaking of the ruined land of Edom as if **it** were **a habitation of jackals**, a place fit only for wild animals to live. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and jackals will make their homes there]

The **jackals** are a kind of wild animal, similar to a small wolf. If your readers would not be familiar with what jackals are, you could use the name of a similar animal that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [wild dogs]

Isaiah is using **the daughters of the ostrich** as a common expression of the culture to mean “ostriches.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [for ostriches]

14.note: The terms **desert creatures** and **hyenas** refer to kinds of wild animals that live in desolate places. If your readers would not be familiar with what they are, you could use the names of similar animals that your readers would recognize, or you could use more general terms. Alternate translation: [And wild animals will meet scavengers]

If the connection between this statement and the previous one is not clear, you may want to use a different connecting word to show how this statement relates to what comes before it. Alternate translation: [Also]

A **night creature** is a kind of animal that is active at night, though its exact identity is uncertain. If your readers would not be familiar with what this is, you could use the name of a similar animal that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [a creature that comes out at night]

15.note: A **great owl** is a kind of bird. If your readers would not be familiar with what this is, you could use the name of a similar bird that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [a large owl]
The pronoun **its** refers to the ruins described in previous verse. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [shade left in the destroyed land]

If the connection between this statement and the previous one is not clear, you may want to use a different connecting word to show how this statement relates to what comes before it. Alternate translation: [In fact, hawks will also gather]

The term **hawks** describes a kind of bird of prey. If your readers would not be familiar with what hawks are, you could use the name of a similar bird that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general expression. Alternate translation: [birds of prey]

The expression **will be gathered** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [hawks will gather there]

Isaiah is using a common expression of his culture that is usually “a man and his companion,” meaning “each person and his fellow person.” He is using feminine forms
for “each” and “companion” since the terms for the birds he names are feminine. This expression does not mean “a bird and her mate.” The UST models one way to represent the meaning.

16.note: The word translated as **Seek** is an imperative, but it communicates a condition rather than a command. If the imperative does not communicate a condition for your readers, then use a form in your language that communicates a condition. Alternate translation: [If you seek from upon the scroll of Yahweh and read]
The pronoun **it** refers to the mouth of Yahweh. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [for my mouth has commanded]

16.q: כִּֽי־פִ⁠י֙ ה֣וּא צִוָּ֔ה וְ⁠רוּח֖⁠וֹ ה֥וּא קִבְּצָֽ⁠ן
16.note: Isaiah is repeating the pronouns **he** and **it** in order to intensify his expression of the ideas that they convey. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [since my mouth, it, my mouth itself, has commanded, and his Spirit, he himself has gathered]

Here, **my mouth** represents “what I have spoken.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [what I have spoken has given the command]

17.note: Isaiah is repeating the pronoun **he** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [And it is Yahweh, he himself, who has cast the lot]

Isaiah is using **cast the lot** as a common expression of the culture to mean “assigned each of them its portion.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And he assigned each of them their portion]

Here, **his hand** represents Yahweh acting with his own power. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [he, by his power, has divided for them by a measuring line]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **generation**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [their children and their children’s children,]
